tasks.spreadsheet:
Build an excellent desktop business intelligence report from the local shared CSV files. This is fictional data. Work autonomously using file and shell tools. Do not read other conditions or grader files. Use only these inputs and this task. No internet research is needed.

Deliver in your assigned output directory: index.html (standalone, visually polished, functional charts and filtering), analysis.py or analysis.js (reproducible calculations), results.json (schema below), and a short methodology.txt. All report assets must be local or embedded. Serve/report URLs should work through the existing HTTP server. Prefer a dark editorial dashboard, restrained electric-blue accents, clear large numeric charts, generous spacing and real working controls. Exactly THREE prominent business insights, each with numeric evidence and a sensible action. Show source counts and data handling. Do not confuse revenue with profit. Check arithmetic using code. Inspect the output and perform one self-review before finishing. Desktop first.

Accounting rules: deduplicate orders by order_id (duplicates are identical); only paid orders count. Net revenue = gross_cents - discount_cents - all matched refund amounts. Contribution = net revenue - cogs_cents - fulfilment_cents. Refunds belong to their original order date. ROAS = net revenue / ad spend and is NOT profit or incremental marketing lift. All amounts use integer cents, shown as USD in UI. Ad spend includes all dates in the period. Never subtract ad spend for the country contribution metric. Q3 is July–September; Q4 is October–December. No extrapolation to other periods.

The three requested insights: (1) Q4 versus Q3 net revenue: dollar change and percent growth. (2) Country with highest total contribution dollars, including its net revenue, contribution and contribution margin. (3) Channel with highest net-revenue ROAS, including its net revenue, spend and ROAS, with the caveat that attribution is not causation.

results.json schema (numeric values unrounded except displayed UI):
{"counts":{"raw_orders":0,"unique_orders":0,"paid_orders":0,"duplicates_removed":0,"refund_rows":0},"quarter":{"q3_net_cents":0,"q4_net_cents":0,"change_cents":0,"growth_pct":0},"country":{"name":"","net_cents":0,"contribution_cents":0,"margin_pct":0},"channel":{"name":"","net_cents":0,"spend_cents":0,"roas":0},"insights":["exactly three supported insights"]}

Do not spend time on mobile testing or image generation. A report is incomplete if it invents numbers, has nonworking filter controls, or omits these deliverables. The input files live in the sibling shared directory supplied in your launch prompt.
tasks.documents:
Use the substantial document or document pack selected by Jack. If no source is attached or selected, first list up to three suitable long PDFs on the Desktop by filename and page count, then let Jack choose before uploading any private content to an external model. Use the identical selected source for all conditions. Preserve the original files.

Create a two-page decision brief plus an evidence table answering these ten questions: What is the main proposal? What decisions are requested? What are the stated objectives? What dates and milestones matter? What resources or costs are specified? What assumptions does the proposal rely on? What risks are explicitly acknowledged? What evidence supports the claimed benefits? Where do sections contradict each other or leave gaps? What still needs clarification before a decision?

Every answer must cite the PDF page and a short locating phrase. Separate source statements from your interpretation. Say when the document does not answer a question. Check assertions across distant sections. Do not invent contradictions. Do not rely on outside knowledge or web search. Preserve table units and qualifiers. Deliver the brief as a PDF, the evidence table as CSV and a short list of unsupported questions. Verify ten citations against the original pages. Record extracted input token count; page count is not a token count.
